A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same work, Decision Tree Learning on Product Spaces, with all 22 pages and Appendices A–E available. Full-text comparison and page rendering establish that pages 2–22 are identical; differences are confined to first-page author and version information.

before.justification: Appendix D and Figure 2 report original experiments evaluating Algorithm 2 on synthetic Boolean decision-tree targets, including recovered tree sizes and query counts over six independent repetitions.

after.justification: Appendix D and Figure 2 retain the same original experiments, reporting recovered tree sizes and query counts for synthetic Boolean decision-tree targets over six independent repetitions.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 retain identical splitting, score estimation, leaf labeling, sample augmentation, and termination procedures.

E1.justification: Appendix D retains the same balanced and unbalanced synthetic Boolean targets and product distributions with coordinate probabilities 0.5, 0.3, and 0.1. No evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Appendix D evaluates Algorithm 2 without competing learning methods in both versions. References to other algorithms remain contextual or theoretical comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix D and Figure 2 retain identical accuracy and dimension sweeps, target sizes, confidence parameters, sampling procedures, and evaluation measures.

E4.justification: The experiments varying accuracy, dimension, distribution bias, and target structure are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report means across six independent repetitions with error bars representing plus or minus one standard deviation in Appendix D and Figure 2.

E6.justification: Figure 2's tree-size and query-count curves and error bars are identical, as are Appendix D's reported findings. No result entries or values change.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, theoretical guarantees, and derivations in Sections 3–5, the proofs in Appendix C, and the worked examples in Appendix E are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about guarantees under arbitrary product distributions, depth-dependent size bounds, and a parameter-free implementation.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the depth parameters and empirical findings are unchanged, along with the pruning limitation and proposed extensions beyond Boolean product spaces in Sections 7–8.

D1.justification: Section 5 and Appendices B and D retain identical implementation, pseudocode, sampling, and experimental disclosures. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to earlier decision-tree research in Sections 1–2 and Appendix A are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first author's name changes from Arshia Soltani Moakahr to Arshia Soltani Moakhar. The arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 13 May 2026 to v2 dated 18 June 2026; the remaining wording and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2, algorithm displays, captions, and page layout remain unchanged. Pages 2–22 render identically; first-page differences concern author and version text.

improvement.justification: The later version corrects the first author's name and updates the version/date information. Scientific content, proofs, empirical evidence, explanations, and reproducibility information remain identical, so these editorial changes do not meaningfully alter the paper's overall quality.
